clue.text: Party is able to keep car for Republican

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the car sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
is able means can
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: A partygoer can drive a car on behalf of a Republican cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' with a capital means a citizen of a republic, here the Dominican Republic, not a member of the US party.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Dominican Republic is literally a citizen of that republic, hence a Republican in this playful sense.

clue.text: State of revolution in Asia, Buddhist-inspired

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters found are read backwards
the answer lies inside the words Asia and Buddhist

explanation.surface: A country in Asia undergoing a revolution inspired by Buddhism.
explanation.walkthrough: The run IABUD sits across 'Asia, Buddhist'; turned round it gives the answer. 'inspired' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the emirates making up the United Arab Emirates, so a constituent state.

clue.text: Sporting imitation heather

parts.note: a model is a copy or imitation of something
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: An imitation heather plant being used for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' is not about games: to sport clothes is to wear and show them off, as a fashion model does.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing off clothes on the catwalk is wearing or displaying them, a sense of sporting garments.

clue.text: Coiner has counterfeit logo inset

indicators.note: counterfeit means faked, so the letters of logo inset are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A forger of coins has put a fake logo into his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coiner' suggests a forger of money, fitting 'counterfeit', but here it is a coiner of new words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invents new words or phrases is said to coin them, so is a coiner.

clue.text: Charge spy employed as bookmaker

parts.note: a commission is a fee charged for a service
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A spy employed to place bets is paid a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission agent is an old term for a bookie who takes bets on commission.

clue.text: Leaving aside social position means "all the same"

parts.note: leaving something aside is not going with it, read as not with
standing is status or social position

explanation.surface: Ignoring rank, everyone is treated equally.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means nevertheless, so it is a synonym of all the same.

clue.text: Confound supporter of bail

definitions.meaning: in cricket the bails rest on top of the three upright wooden posts at the wicket

explanation.surface: Perplexing a court with someone who stands bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bail' suggests a court, but it is a cricket bail, a small crosspiece resting on the posts of the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle them; a cricket stump holds up the bails.

clue.text: Starts to seem pushy, after greeting a cavalryman

indicators.note: the starting letters are followed by the remaining pieces
the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Someone seems pushy after greeting a horse soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A spahi was a Turkish or later French-Algerian cavalry soldier.

clue.text: When about 50, one is not switched on

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for one goes round the number

parts.note: a unit is one of something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: At fifty, a person is no longer turned on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp or fire that is unlit has not been turned on or lighted.

clue.text: Beam in doorway needs painting

indicators.note: the beam is placed inside the doorway

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway or entrance
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A wooden beam in a doorway needs a coat of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a timber and 'painting' as decorating; they are a ray of light and a depiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction of someone, as a painted picture is.

clue.text: Litter area round sleepers

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals, so a bed
room means space or area

explanation.surface: Rubbish is spread over the area around railway sleepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepers' suggests railway track and 'litter' rubbish; the sleepers are people and the definition is the room around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where people sleep surrounds them as they lie asleep.

clue.text: It shows what can appear on your screen

definitions.text: It shows what can appear on your screen

parts.words: It shows what can appear on your screen
parts.note: a short advertisement for a film previews what will be shown at the cinema

explanation.definitionFit: A film preview offers clips of a picture coming soon to the screen.

clue.text: John accompanies soldier returning home in the cold

indicators.note: returning means the word for the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
john is slang for a lavatory, as is loo

explanation.surface: John goes with a soldier coming back home through the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is a dwelling built in freezing climates.

clue.text: Duty list I can start to inveigh about, being the originator

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the first letter of inveigh is taken

explanation.surface: A duty roster lets me begin complaining, as the instigator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run ROTAITINI round.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiator is someone who starts something off, so its originator.

clue.text: Old politician taken in by excellent excuse

indicators.note: the politician is contained by the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-class; the 1 is read as the letter I
Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of the old British Liberal Party

explanation.surface: A former politician is fooled by a superb excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent, and its 1 stands as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse.

clue.text: Concession offering discount

explanation.definitionFit: Making allowance is granting something; an allowance off a bill is a reduction.

clue.text: Discipline regressive lout Flashman, for example?

parts.note: to school is to train or discipline

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for lout is reversed

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout

explanation.surface: Disciplining a backward lout, like a certain bully.
explanation.walkthrough: Flashman is the bully in Tom Brown's Schooldays, a classic English public-school novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashman is a pupil at Rugby School in the novel, an example of a boy at school.

clue.text: Apply ointment here immediately

definitions.meaning: rub cream directly on the affected place

explanation.surface: Instructions on a tube of cream: apply at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to the precise place, or done straight away: both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: It helps travellers overseas after derailment

definitions.text: It helps travellers overseas after derailment

parts.words: It helps travellers overseas after derailment
parts.note: a service connecting with a ferry carries passengers to a port; read as boat plus railway service

explanation.definitionFit: A rail service timed to meet a ship carries passengers on to sail abroad.

clue.text: Rushes off to get crossword answers published

parts.note: lights are the answers entered in a crossword grid
out means published, as a book is out

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to see their crossword solutions printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light out' is informal for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To light out is a colloquialism for departing quickly.

clue.text: Use net to catch troll

definitions.meaning: drag a net to haul in fish
fish by drawing a line through the water

explanation.surface: Netting a troll from under the bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troll' suggests the monster; it is fishing with a trailed line.
explanation.definitionFit: Trawling is dragging a net to catch fish, and loosely also fishing by trolling.

clue.text: Shrinking from the unending raw wind in resort

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the word the is dropped

explanation.surface: Retreating from the bitter winds at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims THE to TH; 'in resort' rearranges TH, RAW and WIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawn describes someone shy and retiring, shrinking from company.

clue.text: Historian no American understood

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters for American are removed

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian

explanation.surface: No American historian understood it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being stated.

clue.text: Song, rather scrappy, needing intro changed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word must be swapped for another

parts.note: bitty means made of scraps, scrappy

explanation.surface: A song so fragmented it needs a new opening.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTY has its intro B changed to D.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditty is a short simple song.

clue.text: Bar full of drunken poets

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters of poets are mixed

explanation.surface: A pub full of drunken poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a pub; it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term for barring someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Note written in temper is insignificant in some cases

indicators.note: the note is set inside the word for temper

parts.note: a pet is a fit of bad temper
ti is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered note matters little in some instances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' are law cases: in legal terms such as petit jury the word means small or minor.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal usage petit means minor or petty, as in petit larceny.

clue.text: Band of the old American school, perhaps

definitions.text: Band of the old American school, perhaps

parts.words: Band of the old American school, perhaps
parts.note: an old school tie is the band of fabric worn round the throat, the term being chiefly American

explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth worn round the neck, as with a school tie, is a classic American word.

clue.text: Establish factory by motorway, given backing

indicators.note: backing means reversing, so the motorway's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its 1 serves as I
a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A factory is set up beside the motorway with financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is read as MI, Britain's first long motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant an idea is to fix or establish it firmly.

clue.text: Guardsman first to leave the field

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word departs

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: The leading guard leaves the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' is not a meadow but the runners in a race, all its entrants.
explanation.definitionFit: The entry for a race is the list of competitors, collectively the field.

clue.text: Firmly closed purse, being well organised

parts.note: tight means firmly closed or sealed
to purse the brows is to knit them

explanation.surface: A purse closed firmly, as with a careful saver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purse' is the verb, as in pursing or knitting one's brows.
explanation.definitionFit: A closely integrated group is tightly structured, so well organised.
